newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine automakers warn on unpaid VAT credits.
newsitem.headline: Argentine automakers warn on unpaid VAT credits.

text.p: Argentine carmakers said Wednesday the build-up of debts owed them by the state, mostly in the form of unpaid tax credits, could force them to cut back their imports and exports.

"This is reaching levels where it will oblige us to put the brakes on export and import activity in order to reduce it, because company chiefs here have debt limits set by their headquarters," said ADEFA car lobby president Horacio Losoviz.

Under Argentina's auto industry regime, the state gives manufacturers value added tax credits on exports and charges VAT on imports immediately. This has led to a build-up of tax credits of $560 million, Losoviz told reporters.
"We cannot give that much free financing to the state," the industry lobby leader told local radio.
Argentina's Industry Ministry said Wednesday it would soon pay up $50 million of debts with the auto industry and was in the process of studying mechanisms to pay $100 million more.
Jorge Sandullo, head of the DGI tax agency, said the remaining debt was "the difference between credits and debits which is what happens to anyone who pays VAT in this country."
